lajc-06-au-festival-des-sciences-de-nice.title: AJC06 at the Nice Science Festival – 2025
lajc-06-au-festival-des-sciences-de-nice.excerpt: Once again this year, AJC06 took part in the Science Festival organised by Université Côte d'Azur and its partners, bringing researchers, students and the public together to share the scientific method and spark critical thinking.
lajc-06-au-festival-des-sciences-de-nice.body:
Once again this year, **AJC06** took part in the **Science Festival** organised by **Université Côte d'Azur** and its partners. The event brought researchers, students and the general public together around a shared goal: **sharing the scientific method and sparking critical thinking**.

### Understanding how scientific knowledge is built

On our stand, visitors could explore and discuss several playful teaching materials:

- a **poster on how knowledge is built**, tracing the steps of the scientific process, from formulating a hypothesis to publishing results;
- a **pyramid of evidence**, explaining the hierarchy of sources and how researchers assess how reliable knowledge is;
- a poster on **the difference between a journalist's work and a researcher's**, to understand how information travels and changes between academia and the media;
- a game showing the diversity of scientific disciplines, from history to physics by way of anthropology.

These tools sparked many conversations with school groups and families who came to explore science in all its forms.

We are happy to share the resources we used, for anyone who may find them useful.

---

### Promoting research and young researchers

As an association of PhD candidates and early-career researchers, AJC06 is committed to **making research accessible** and **showcasing the diversity of disciplines** at Université Côte d'Azur.
Taking part in the Science Festival is also a chance for us to **show what the job of a researcher really looks like**, something often little known, and to remind everyone that science is above all a **collective, rigorous adventure that is open to society**.

[Poster from the Fête de la science (in French)](/media/documents/2025-10-poster-fete-de-la-science-2-1-1.pdf)

mediation-scientifique-serious-game-sur-.title: Science outreach: a serious game about the researcher's journey
mediation-scientifique-serious-game-sur-.excerpt: At the Nice Science Festival, AJC06 presented original games that explain the long road from high school to a permanent research position.
mediation-scientifique-serious-game-sur-.body:
AJC06 – the Association of Young Researchers of the Alpes-Maritimes – had the opportunity to take part in the Nice Science Festival.

For the occasion, Gwenaëlle Prigent created an outreach tool to demystify the path to becoming a researcher.

To make it fun, we designed original games that explain the long road from the baccalauréat to a permanent research position.

The goal? To help people of all ages better understand the steps, the challenges, and also the small moments of joy that punctuate a PhD candidate's life.

AJC06 makes this tool freely available to everyone to reuse.

[The researcher's journey game (PDF, in French)](/media/documents/2024-10-jeu-parcours-chercheur-3.pdf)

stage-initiation-alpinisme-2024.title: Introduction to mountaineering 2024
stage-initiation-alpinisme-2024.excerpt: Université Côte d'Azur's mountaineering club is running introductory sessions again: rope work, belaying and rock, snow and mixed routes in the Mercantour.
stage-initiation-alpinisme-2024.body:
Université Côte d'Azur's mountaineering club, "UniCA mountaineering", is once again offering introductory mountaineering sessions, covering the fundamentals (the rope and belaying skills that are essential in high mountains) and progressing on rock, snow and mixed routes in the stunning Mercantour!
In partnership with high-mountain guides (Guide06).
The aim of these sessions is to help participants become independent.

A maximum of 5 places per session, so be quick!
